clue.text: Show muscle in rejection of the foreign musical

indicators.note: the muscle word is set inside the reversed run, so in signals a container here
a rejection throws something back, so the foreign article and the musical are read backwards together

parts.note: EL is 'the' in Spanish, a foreign language
CATS is the long-running Lloyd Webber musical
PEC is short for pectoral, a chest muscle

explanation.surface: A bodybuilder flexes in protest at a foreign musical being turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejection of' turns the Spanish article and the musical round as one run, giving STACLE; 'in' sets the muscle after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectacle is a striking public display, so it is a synonym for a show.

clue.text: Use power to break forward

indicators.note: one piece breaks into another, splitting it open, so this marks a container

parts.note: to forward a letter is to send it on
P is the standard abbreviation for power in physics

explanation.surface: An instruction to apply force to smash through towards the front.
explanation.definitionFit: To spend something is to use it up, a straightforward verb synonym.

clue.text: Just a few words, but right to intervene

indicators.note: to intervene is to come between, so one letter is placed within the other word

parts.note: 'but' in the sense of 'other than' means except

explanation.surface: Someone says only a little, but rightly steps in to intervene.
explanation.definitionFit: An excerpt is a short extract quoted from a longer text, a few words only.

clue.text: Entrance which may be public?

definitions.meaning: as a verb, to entrance someone is to carry them away with delight, to enrapture
buses and trains form a public system for moving people about

explanation.definitionFit: Transport as a verb means to enrapture, and as a noun it is the system that can be public.

clue.text: Food arrives? Cat disheartened

parts.note: arrives means comes

indicators.note: losing the heart means losing a central letter of the cat's name

parts.note: Tibbles is a stock British name for a pet cat

explanation.surface: Dinner is served, but the cat has lost its spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disheartened' removes one of the two middle Bs from TIBBLES, a classic British pet cat's name, leaving TIBLES.
explanation.definitionFit: Comestibles is a formal or jocular word for things to eat, so it means food.

clue.text: Newt hurried off, having wiped brow

indicators.note: the brow is the top, so in a down entry the first letter is wiped away

parts.note: someone who hurried off has left

explanation.surface: A small amphibian dashed away after mopping its forehead.
explanation.definitionFit: An eft is an old or dialect name for a newt, a common crossword creature.

clue.text: Bust — or not? There's seconds in it!

indicators.note: the clue says the seconds are in it, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: the stock phrase 'boom or bust' makes boom the opposite of bust

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a chest is real, noticing extra helpings inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bust — or not?' asks for the alternative to bust in the economic phrase 'boom or bust', giving BOOM.
explanation.definitionFit: Bosom and bust are both words for a woman's chest, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Discard, then move in simple game

parts.note: to bin something is to throw it away
go means to move

explanation.surface: Throw away a card and then take your turn in an easy game.
explanation.definitionFit: Bingo is a simple game of chance played by marking off called numbers.

clue.text: Dud titters, seeing fugal devices

indicators.note: a dud version of the word is a failed one, so its letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: Feeble giggles greet some musical tricks in a fugue.
explanation.definitionFit: Stretti are overlapping entries of the subject in a fugue, a contrapuntal technique.

clue.text: Me and old bird hoarding foreign money in notes

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: to hoard is to keep something stored within, so the bird holds the money

parts.note: the moa is an extinct flightless bird of New Zealand
the rand is the currency of South Africa

explanation.surface: A person and an elderly companion stash foreign cash in banknotes.
explanation.definitionFit: Memoranda, plural of memorandum, are written notes or reminders.

clue.text: Cry, as individual pierces old shellfish

parts.note: EX means former, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: to pierce is to go into, so the single letter enters the shellfish

parts.note: a clam is a bivalve shellfish
I, the roman numeral one, stands for a single individual

explanation.surface: Someone shouts as a lone figure stabs into an elderly mollusc.
explanation.definitionFit: To exclaim is to cry out suddenly, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Beat the instrument, not the dog, showing fit of temper

parts.note: to tan someone's hide is to beat them

indicators.note: the instrument is to be taken without the dog part, so those letters go

parts.note: the trumpet is a brass instrument
a pet dog, so the dog stands for PET

explanation.surface: Someone thrashes a musical instrument rather than the dog in a rage.
explanation.definitionFit: A tantrum is an outburst of bad temper, a synonym for a fit of temper.

clue.text: Italian masterpiece read as if Arabic? It's a game

indicators.note: Arabic script runs right to left, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a Strad is a Stradivarius violin, a masterpiece of Italian craftsmanship

explanation.surface: A classic Italian work misread as Arabic turns out to be a mere game.
explanation.definitionFit: Darts is a pub game of throwing pointed missiles at a board, an example of a game.

clue.text: One sharpening teeth, being monstrous to cowards

indicators.note: monstrous suggests something misshapen, so these letters are deformed into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone baring sharpened fangs is being a monster to the timid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being' is a link word. 'teeth' suggests fangs, but they are the teeth of a saw.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw doctor is a tradesman who sharpens and sets the teeth of saws.

clue.text: Extended arm about to grab sparkling drink — here?

definitions.text: Extended arm about to grab sparkling drink — here?

indicators.note: the arm is extended, stretched out to make room for other letters
the arm goes about, around, the other pieces

parts.note: a wing is an arm of a building or an organisation
to net something is to catch or grab it
Asti is a sparkling Italian wine

explanation.surface: A hand reaches out for a glass of fizz at a gathering of wine lovers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extended' and 'about' together make the arm wrap round the other two pieces, and the whole clue also paints the scene being defined.
explanation.definitionFit: At a wine tasting people reach out for glasses of wine, which is the picture the clue paints.

clue.text: Morsel which is between one's teeth?

definitions.meaning: a morsel is a small piece of food
a horse's bridle mouthpiece sits between its teeth

explanation.definitionFit: Bit means a small piece, and the bit of a bridle sits in a horse's mouth.

clue.text: Ultimately, hospital cuts behind relapse

indicators.note: the letter cuts into the larger word, splitting it

parts.note: a backside is one's behind or bottom

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so the last letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: In the end hospital spending cuts lead back to a decline.
explanation.definitionFit: To backslide is to relapse into bad habits, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Tendency that is to introduce books in speech

indicators.note: the first pieces are introduced into the speech, placed inside it

parts.note: an oration is a formal speech
IE abbreviates id est, Latin for that is
NT, the New Testament, is a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: Someone tends to mention reading matter during a talk.
explanation.walkthrough: The second 'in' is only a link; 'to introduce' is what puts the two abbreviations inside the speech.
explanation.definitionFit: An orientation is a bent or leaning, such as a political tendency.

clue.text: Boy about to shut out star

indicators.note: the boy's name goes round the verb, so it is a container

parts.note: Alan is a boy's name
to debar is to exclude or shut out

explanation.surface: A lad is on the point of excluding a celebrity.
explanation.definitionFit: Aldebaran is a bright red giant, the brightest star in Taurus.

clue.text: New deal cut to save a mine that's caved in

indicators.note: to save something is to keep it safe within, so the scrambled letters hold the rest
a new form of these letters is a rearrangement

parts.note: a pit is a coal mine

explanation.surface: A fresh agreement on cuts is meant to rescue a collapsed colliery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' rearranges DEAL CUT into C...ULATED, which holds A + PIT; 'that's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To capitulate is to give in or surrender, so caved in means capitulated.

clue.text: Story going over one's head?

definitions.meaning: porky pie is rhyming slang for lie, a story or fib
a hat with a flat crown worn on the head

explanation.walkthrough: In British rhyming slang 'pork pie' (or porky) means a lie; the pork-pie hat sits over your head.
explanation.definitionFit: Porky pie is Cockney rhyming slang for a lie, and a pork pie is also a style of hat.

clue.text: Meal instead's drunk

indicators.note: drunk in the sense of taken in, so the answer is held within the word

explanation.surface: Someone has a cuppa in place of eating.
explanation.definitionFit: Tea is a light afternoon or evening meal in Britain, besides being the drink.

clue.text: Potential disaster with theatre's opening, as star announces himself?

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the Sun is a star
announcing himself, a character might declare 'am I' after his name, in an inverted poetic order

explanation.surface: A theatre debut risks catastrophe when the lead introduces himself.
explanation.walkthrough: A star introducing itself in old-fashioned inverted word order says 'Sun am I', and that phrase follows the theatre's first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A tidal wave is a natural disaster waiting to happen.

clue.text: King stops to drink milk from these, which is tops

indicators.note: the letter stops up, plugs, the verb by sitting inside it

parts.note: to sup is to drink
R stands for rex, Latin for king
asses' milk is the famous bathing milk of Cleopatra

explanation.surface: A monarch halts to drink donkeys' milk, which beats everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'which is' is a link to the definition 'tops' as a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To top something is to exceed it, so surpasses means tops.

clue.text: Perhaps float up

indicators.note: perhaps flags that the word is just one possible arrangement of its letters

explanation.surface: Something might drift upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Aloft means up in the air, an adverbial synonym.

clue.text: Certain books are

definitions.meaning: ... to happen means certain to happen

explanation.definitionFit: Bound means certain, as in bound to win, and books are bound by a binder.

clue.text: Head of state halving tax, appearing pale

indicators.note: the letter cuts the tax word into two halves, sitting between them

parts.note: a duty is a tax on goods

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: The head of government cuts tax in half and looks wan.
explanation.definitionFit: Dusty colours are greyish and faded, so dusty can mean pale.

clue.text: Wicked Zulus strip outside of house

parts.note: an impi is a regiment of Zulu warriors

indicators.note: stripping the outside of a word removes its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Bad Zulus strip the exterior of a dwelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Impious means lacking reverence for God, hence wicked.

clue.text: Runner starts to sprint, keeping impetus

indicators.note: the starts of each of the following words give their first letters

explanation.surface: An athlete begins a dash, maintaining momentum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runner' suggests an athlete, but a ski runs over snow.
explanation.definitionFit: A ski is a runner, as on a sledge, a long blade gliding over snow.

clue.text: Where the Department of Transport might invest, causing intrusions

definitions.text: Where the Department of Transport might invest
definitions.meaning: a transport ministry spends its money on the highways

explanation.walkthrough: 'causing' is a link between the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Inroads are incursions or encroachments, and read as 'in roads' they are a transport budget.

clue.text: Ordinal has covers torn off ———- it happens

indicators.note: the covers are the outer letters, so the first and last are removed

parts.note: seventh is an ordinal number

explanation.surface: A numbered position loses its outer wrapping, as these things do.
explanation.definitionFit: An event is something that happens, an occurrence.

clue.text: Roughly one guy in ten showing skill

parts.note: I is the roman numeral one

indicators.note: roughly suggests a rough, imprecise arrangement of the letters

explanation.surface: About one man in ten demonstrates ability.
explanation.walkthrough: 'showing' is a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Ingenuity is cleverness or inventive skill.
